summary: For the target-valid form Q_N=2X1X2+(X3+X4)^2/2 with spectrum {1,-1,1,0} and separated-fragment X3,X4, original-coordinate conditioning plus the physical-pair logarithmic theorem gives ||p_QN||inf<=8sqrt(2) uniformly. Conditioning first on U=X3-X4, normalizing V=X3+X4, and then paying the pair-log square-root curvature certificate yields (32/3)[(1-1/N)sqrt(N)+1/N], diverging as sqrt(N). This refutes only normalize-thin-fiber-then-pair-log averaging; QFORM and the pair-log theorem are not refuted. A safe compiler must retain a full unnormalized slice-mass power through reciprocal-curvature payment.
